rationale: The workflow is a production deployment to Fly.io (push to master, release published, workflow_dispatch) with a single deploy job. The relevant run-cancellation optimization (P-LIT-CANCEL-STALE) is already implemented via `concurrency: deploy-group`, which cancels in-progress/superseded runs in the same group, and that pattern is explicitly contraindicated for release/deployment work anyway. P-LIT-SKIP-WORKFLOW is unsuitable because deploy triggers are required checks and skipping runs would weaken deployment coverage. P-LIT-FAIL-FAST, P-LIT-FAILED-JOB-FIRST, P-LIT-PRIORITIZE, and schedule-based patterns do not apply: there is no matrix, no schedule, and only one job. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT carries the contraindication that valid slow deploys may exceed any proposed limit, and the CI history only shows short successful runs (~2-3 min) without deploy-duration bounds, so adding a timeout risks interrupting legitimate deploys. P-LIT-GHA-CACHE offers only modest, uncertain benefit for already-fast runs and the workflow pins `fetch-depth: 0`; adding a dependency cache is not clearly supported for this deploy workflow. No supported optimization preserves intended build/deploy coverage while being clearly applicable here.
